verdicts.reason: A is a readable vertical stack, but it mixes axes: the logo and CTA are centred while the headline and subcopy hang off a left edge at x≈31. The logo also overpowers a headline that is small for the canvas, and the gaps between blocks are uneven. B scatters its pieces: the headline and subcopy sit top-left, the logo drifts bottom-left and the CTA floats alone at mid-right, so reading order and grouping break down and large dead areas open up.

A has the same flaws as above: centred logo and CTA against left-aligned text, a weak headline under an oversized logo, and uneven vertical gaps. B puts the logo and text on a left axis, but the CTA is indented to x≈127 and almost aligns without lining up. The whole right half of the canvas is empty, which makes the layout lopsided, and the small headline still lacks presence.

A is the same mixed-axis stack (centred logo and CTA, left-aligned text) with an undersized headline. B keeps the banner's logo-left, copy-right relationship, which is more faithful to the original. Its flaws: the headline wraps with 'Monday' orphaned on its own line, the CTA is indented from the text column's left edge, and the text column is narrow beside the large logo.
